channel.title: Relay Updates
channel.description: Signed updates for Relay on macOS.

item.description:
# Relay 0.3.4
Relay now searches beyond the standard Applications folders when an app is not found immediately.
- Adds a one-time background search across additional user-accessible installation locations. - Publishes results progressively and caches discovered applications for later searches. - Shows available software updates directly in the main command window. - Adds Open folder for clipboard entries containing a folder path available on this Mac. Use the row button, Command-Return, or Actions; Copy remains available.
The fast standard application index remains the first search path. Relay starts the broader background search only after an application-search miss.

# Relay 0.3.3
Relay now offers **Automatically download and install future updates** in **Library & Settings → Settings → General → Software Updates**. This option is off by default. Turn on automatic checks first, then enable the new checkbox.
Sparkle verifies updates before installing them. Automatic updates normally install when Relay quits, so an open session is not interrupted. If Relay stays open for a long time or macOS requires authorization, you may be prompted to finish the update. Turning off automatic checks also turns off automatic installation.
The Launch at Login option and System Settings search from earlier releases remain available.

# Relay 0.3.2
Relay can now start automatically when you sign in to your Mac. Open **Library & Settings → Settings → General → This Mac** and turn on **Launch Relay at login**. The switch reflects the current macOS login-item setting; if macOS requires approval, Relay tells you where to finish enabling it.
This release retains the settings search added in 0.3.1 and signed in-app updates. Existing 0.3.x installs can update from **Check for Updates…**; 0.2.0 installs still need one manual installation because they predate the updater.
